MDHHS announces grant funding for rural health workforce initiative in Michigan
S. B. Lam
The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services announced on July 8 that it has issued grant funding opportunities for the Rural Health Transformation Program to support the Workforce for Wellness Initiative.
Michigan’s Rural Health Transformation Program aims to build a strong rural health system that ensures residents have access to high-quality care close to home. The program uses coordinated, community-driven strategies across four main initiatives: strengthening partnerships supporting rural health transformation, expanding and stabilizing the workforce needed for community wellness, advancing interoperability among providers, and developing models that bring essential services closer to where people live.
The Workforce for Wellness Initiative is intended to strengthen Michigan’s rural health workforce and support integrated care delivery. Approximately $34,231,500 will be available through five separate funding opportunities focused on recruitment, retention, and training across various healthcare professions. The initiative seeks to support current professionals serving rural communities while expanding the pipeline of qualified healthcare workers by investing in programs using proven best practices.
The award period begins October 1, 2026, and ends September 30, 2027. Available funding includes $5 million for Maternal Health Provider Training; $7 million for a University-Led Master of Social Work Award Program; $14.73 million for a Rural Health Provider Recruitment and Retention Program; $2.5 million for a Limited License Master of Social Work Supervision Stipend Program; and $5 million for a Bachelor of Social Work to Clinical Master of Social Work Stipend Program.
Eligible applicants include nonprofits with 501(c)(3) status, private or public entities, local health departments, federally recognized Michigan tribes or Indian Health Clinic programs, as well as universities. Project director requests for application access are due by 5 p.m., Thursday, July 30. Grant applications must be submitted electronically through the EGrAMS system by 3 p.m., Tuesday, August 4.
A pre-application conference will take place at 10:00 a.m., Wednesday, July 15 via webinar at https://bit.ly/4p0YU7m. A recording will be posted afterward on the EGrAMS system website along with application instructions under ‘Current Grants’ within Policy and Planning.
This grant opportunity is supported by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services as part of an award totaling over $173 million provided entirely by CMS/HHS.
